tz: 数据库设计与 ER 图

cards.tz: 好的与坏的数据库设计
cards.en:
Intuition: think of a messy school bag. If every worksheet is thrown in one pocket, you find things slowly and keep extra copies "just in case". A database is the same.

The rule: a good design is

  • organised: each table is about one thing (students, classes, subjects);
  • efficient: each fact is stored once;
  • easy to use: tables are linked in a logical way by keys.

A bad design causes slow performance, data inconsistency (two copies of a fact that disagree) and difficulty in retrieving data.

Two tools in this chapter fix this: the ER diagram (plan before building) and normalisation (remove repeated data).

Exam wording: "A well-designed database is organised, efficient and easy to use. Tables are clear and concise, each table contains only the necessary data, and tables are related in a logical way." "A poor design leads to data redundancy, data inconsistency and difficulty in retrieving data."
cards.zh:
直觉：像一个乱糟糟的书包：所有作业塞一格，找东西慢，还会复印很多份"以防万一"。数据库也一样。

规则：好设计要

  • organised：每个表只讲一件事（学生、班、科目）；
  • efficient：每个事实只存一次；
  • easy to use：表之间用 key 合理连接。

坏设计会导致 slow performance、data inconsistency（同一事实两份副本不一致）、difficulty in retrieving data。

本章两大工具：ER diagram（先规划再建表）和 normalisation（去掉重复数据）。

考试写法："A well-designed database is organised, efficient and easy to use..."；"A poor design leads to data redundancy, data inconsistency and difficulty in retrieving data."

ex.q: A shop keeps one big table SALE(SALEID, CNAME, CADDR, CPHONE, ITEM, PRICE). Every sale repeats the customer's address and phone. Give two problems.
ex.a:
1. The same address is stored in many records → data redundancy, wasting storage.
  2. If the customer moves, every record must be changed. Miss one and the database holds two addresses → data inconsistency.
  3. Better: a CUSTOMER table (each customer once) and SALE keeps only the customer ID as a foreign key.
ex.az:
1. 同一地址存很多次 → 冗余浪费空间。
  2. 客户搬家要改很多条，漏改就不一致。
  3. 改进：拆出 CUSTOMER 表，SALE 只存客户 ID（外键）。

ex.q: A library has tables BOOK(BID, TITLE, AUTHOR) and LOAN(BID, MEMBERID, DUEDATE). Is this a good design? Why?
ex.a:
1. Each table is about one thing: books or loans → organised.
  2. Title is stored once in BOOK; LOAN only stores BID → no repeated titles → efficient.
  3. LOAN.BID links to BOOK.BID → related in a logical way.
  4. So it is a good design.
ex.az:
1. 每表只讲一件事。
  2. 书名只在 BOOK 存一次。
  3. 用 BID 合理连接。所以是好设计。

ex.q: A student says: "Storage is cheap now, so repeating data in a table is not a problem." Is this right?
ex.a:
1. Mistake: only thinking about storage space.
  2. The real danger of repeated data is inconsistency: when one copy is updated and another is not, the database gives two different answers.
  3. Repeated data also causes update, insertion and deletion anomalies (section 5.4).
  4. Right answer: redundancy wastes space and risks inconsistent or lost data.
ex.az:
1. 错误：只考虑空间。
  2. 真正问题是不一致：改了一份没改另一份。
  3. 还会造成三种 anomaly（5.4）。
  4. 正确：冗余既浪费空间，也会导致数据不一致或丢失。

demo.query: SELECT SID, SNAME, CLASS, CTEACH FROM STUDENT WHERE CLASS='3B';
demo.note: Bad design: class 3B's teacher is stored in 4 rows. We changed only one row, so 3B now has two different teachers: inconsistent data.

cards.en:
Intuition: an architect draws a plan before building a house. An ER diagram is the plan of a database, drawn before any table is created.

Key words:

  • Entity type: a kind of thing we store data about (Student, Class).
  • Attribute: a property of the entity (Student name).
  • Relationship: how two entity types are linked (Student belongs to Class).

The rule (ER → tables):

  • each entity type → one table
  • each attribute → one field
  • each relationship → a link by foreign key (or an extra table)

Exam wording: "An ER diagram represents the entity types, attributes and relationships of a relational database. It helps decide the table structures before the tables are created."
cards.zh:
直觉：建筑师盖房前先画图。ER diagram 就是数据库的设计图，在建表之前画。

术语：

  • Entity type（实体类型）：要存数据的一类东西（Student、Class）。
  • Attribute（属性）：实体的特征（Student name）。
  • Relationship（关系）：两类实体怎样连（Student belongs to Class）。

规则：entity type → table；attribute → field；relationship → foreign key（或额外的表）。

考试写法："An ER diagram represents the entity types, attributes and relationships of a relational database. It helps decide the table structures before the tables are created."

ex.q: A SCHOOL ER diagram has entity types Student (Student ID underlined, Student name) and Class (Class name underlined, Room number), joined by 'Belong to'. Write the tables.
ex.a:
1. Two rectangles → two tables: STUDENT and CLASS.
  2. Attributes → fields: STUDENT(SID, SNAME), CLASS(CLASSNAME, ROOMNUM).
  3. Underlined → primary keys: SID and CLASSNAME.
  4. 'Belong to' (many students in one class) → add CLASSNAME to STUDENT as a foreign key: STUDENT(SID, SNAME, CLASSNAME).
ex.az:
1. 两个长方形 → 两个表。
  2. 属性 → 字段。
  3. 下划线 → 主键。
  4. Belong to → STUDENT 加外键 CLASSNAME。

ex.q: Textbook Checkpoint 5.1: rectangles Animal, Zone, Species; Animal has ellipses Animal name (underlined), Weight, Date of birth. (a) List the tables. (b) Attributes and primary key of Animal?
ex.a:
1. One table per rectangle: ANIMAL, ZONE, SPECIES.
  2. Animal's attributes: Animal name, Weight, Date of birth.
  3. The underlined one, Animal name, is the primary key.
ex.az:
1. 每个长方形一个表。
  2. Animal 的属性是三个椭圆。
  3. 下划线的 Animal name 是主键。

ex.q: A student writes: "An ER diagram shows the records stored in each table." Correct it.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: an ER diagram shows structure, not data.
  2. It shows entity types, attributes and relationships, i.e. what tables and fields will exist and how they link.
  3. Records (rows such as 'Ada, 3A') never appear in an ER diagram.
ex.az:
1. 错误：ER 图画的是结构，不是数据。
  2. 它只显示实体、属性、关系。
  3. 具体记录不会出现在 ER 图中。

frames.en: Two rectangles: Student and Class. Each will become a table.
frames.zh: 两个长方形 Student、Class，各成一个表。

frames.en: Ellipses: Student ID, Student name; Class name, Room number. Each becomes a field.
The diamond Belong to links them. It becomes a foreign key CLASSNAME in STUDENT.
frames.zh: 菱形 Belong to → STUDENT 中的外键 CLASSNAME。

frames.en:
STUDENT(SID, SNAME, CLASSNAME)
CLASS(CLASSNAME, ROOMNUM)

cards.en:
Intuition: like road signs, each shape has one fixed meaning, so anyone can read the diagram.

ShapeMeansNote
Rectangle ▭Entity typebecomes a table
Diamond ◇Relationshipnamed with a verb: Join, Belong to; may have its own attributes
Ellipse ⬭Attributeunderlined = primary key

Lines join attributes to their entity (or relationship), and entities to diamonds. Colours mean nothing.

How to read: rectangle → diamond → rectangle as a sentence: "Student belongs to Class". From the other side use passive voice: "Zone is managed by Manager".

Exam wording: "Entity types are drawn as rectangles, relationships as diamonds and attributes as ellipses. The primary key attribute is underlined."
cards.zh:
直觉：像交通标志，每个形状意思固定。

形状意思备注
长方形Entity type成为表
菱形Relationship用动词命名；关系也可以有属性
椭圆Attribute下划线 = 主键

线把属性连到实体（或关系），把实体连到菱形。颜色无意义。

读法：长方形→菱形→长方形读成一句话；反方向用被动语态。

考试写法："Entity types are drawn as rectangles, relationships as diamonds and attributes as ellipses. The primary key attribute is underlined."

ex.q: Ellipse 'Treatment date' is connected to the diamond 'Treat' between Doctor and Patient. What does it mean?
ex.a:
1. The ellipse is joined to a diamond, not a rectangle.
  2. So Treatment date is an attribute of the relationship Treat.
  3. Meaning: each time a doctor treats a patient, the date of that treatment is recorded. It belongs to neither doctor nor patient alone.
ex.az:
1. 椭圆连在菱形上。
  2. 所以是关系 Treat 的属性。
  3. 每次某医生治疗某病人的日期。

ex.q: Read the diagram Zone ◇Be managed by◇ Manager as two sentences.
ex.a:
1. Left to right: "A zone is managed by a manager."
  2. Right to left (active voice): "A manager manages a zone."
ex.az:
1. Zone is managed by Manager。
  2. Manager manages Zone。

ex.q: A student draws the entity type Teacher as an ellipse and the attribute Teacher name as a rectangle, and colours keys red. What is wrong?
ex.a:
1. Mistake 1: shapes are swapped. Entity type = rectangle, attribute = ellipse.
  2. Mistake 2: colour has no meaning. The primary key is shown by underlining the attribute.
ex.az:
1. 形状反了：实体是长方形，属性是椭圆。
  2. 颜色没意义，主键要加下划线。

frames.en: Doctor and Patient are rectangles = entity types = tables.
frames.zh: 长方形 = 实体 = 表。

frames.en: Treat is a diamond = relationship: "Doctor treats Patient".
Doctor ID (underlined = PK) on Doctor; Treatment date on the diamond = attribute of the relationship.
frames.zh: 椭圆 = 属性；下划线 = 主键；连在菱形上 = 关系的属性。

cards.t: From ER diagram to table structure and schema
cards.tz: 由 ER 图写出表结构与 schema
cards.en:
Intuition: the ER diagram is the plan; the table structure is the real thing you build in SQL.

Steps:

  1. Each rectangle → a table with a short UPPER-CASE name.
  2. Each ellipse → a field with a short name (Event start time → STARTTIME).
  3. Pick a data type: Character, Integer, Date, Time, Datetime.
  4. Underlined attribute → primary key.
  5. Add foreign keys from the relationships (see 5.3).

A schema is a one-line summary of a table: CLASS(CLASSNAME, ROOMNUM), primary key underlined.

To add a new table to a design: draw a new rectangle with its ellipses, then a diamond linking it to the related entity.

Exam wording: "Each entity type becomes a table and each attribute becomes a field. The underlined attribute is the primary key."
cards.zh:
直觉：ER 图是蓝图，table structure 是用 SQL 真正建出来的东西。

步骤：

  1. 长方形 → 表（大写短名）。
  2. 椭圆 → 字段（短名）。
  3. 选 data type：Character、Integer、Date、Time、Datetime。
  4. 下划线 → 主键。
  5. 按关系加外键（5.3）。

Schema 是表的一行摘要：CLASS(CLASSNAME, ROOMNUM)，主键加下划线。

新增表：画新长方形和椭圆，再用菱形连到相关实体。

考试写法："Each entity type becomes a table and each attribute becomes a field. The underlined attribute is the primary key."

ex.q: Entity Event has attributes Event ID (underlined), Event name, Event start time, Venue. Write the schema and data types.
ex.a:
1. Name the table EVENT; short field names EID, ENAME, STARTTIME, VENUE.
  2. Schema: EVENT(EID, ENAME, STARTTIME, VENUE).
  3. Types: EID Integer, ENAME Character, STARTTIME Datetime, VENUE Character.
  4. See the code block for the CREATE TABLE.
ex.az:
1. 表名 EVENT，字段简称。
  2. 写 schema，主键 EID 下划线。
  3. 选数据类型。

ex.q: A zoo adds Manager (Staff ID underlined, Manager name, Phone, Working hours) to manage zones. How do you add it to the ER diagram?
ex.a:
1. Draw a rectangle Manager.
  2. Draw four ellipses joined to it; underline Staff ID.
  3. Draw a diamond Be managed by between Zone and Manager.
  4. Schema: MANAGER(STAFFID, MNAME, PHONE, WORKHRS).
ex.az:
1. 画长方形 Manager。
  2. 四个椭圆，Staff ID 下划线。
  3. 菱形 Be managed by 连到 Zone。

ex.q: A student writes the schema as EVENT(EID, ENAME, STARTTIME, VENUE) with no underline, and gives STARTTIME the type Character. What is wrong?
ex.a:
1. Mistake 1: the primary key must be underlined in a schema: EVENT(EID, ...).
  2. Mistake 2: a start time stored as Character cannot be sorted or compared correctly (e.g. '9:00' > '10:00' as text). Use Datetime or Time.
ex.az:
1. schema 主键要下划线。
  2. 时间用 Character 无法正确排序比较，应用 Datetime/Time。

notes.t: Create a table called EVENT (from the entity type Event).
notes.tz: 建表 EVENT（来自实体 Event）。

notes.t: EID: integer field; PRIMARY KEY because Event ID is underlined.
ENAME: text up to 30 characters.
notes.tz: ENAME 文本，最多 30 字符。

notes.t: STARTTIME: date and time of the event.
VENUE: text up to 30 characters.
End of the table definition.
Add one sample record.
Show all records to check.

cards.t: Foreign keys are shown by relationships
cards.tz: 外键用关系表示，不画成属性
cards.en:
Intuition: on a map you draw a road between two towns; you don't write the other town's name inside each town. A relationship diamond is the road.

The rule: in an ER diagram, a foreign key is NOT drawn as an ellipse. The link is shown by the relationship. Which table gets the foreign key is decided later, from the cardinality (FK goes on the many side).

Example: LETTER(LID, RADD, PID, MID) with PID → POSTMAN, MID → MAILBOX. Letter only has ellipses Letter ID and Recipient address; diamonds Deliver and Originate from link it to Postman and Mailbox.

Exam wording: "Foreign keys are represented by relationships, not by attributes, in an ER diagram."
cards.zh:
直觉：地图上两城之间画一条路，而不是把对方城名写在城里。菱形就是那条路。

规则：ER 图中外键不画成椭圆，而是用relationship表示。外键放哪个表，建表时按基数决定（放在 many 一方）。

例：LETTER(LID, RADD, PID, MID)，Letter 只画 Letter ID 和 Recipient address 两个椭圆，用菱形 Deliver、Originate from 连 Postman、Mailbox。

考试写法："Foreign keys are represented by relationships, not by attributes, in an ER diagram."

ex.q: PRODUCT(PID, PNAME, PRICE, SID), SID references STORE. A student draws an ellipse 'Store ID' on Product. Correct it.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: drawing the foreign key SID as an attribute of Product.
  2. Remove the 'Store ID' ellipse from Product.
  3. Draw a diamond Sell between Store and Product (Store 1 — M Product).
  4. Store Id stays only as Store's own (underlined) key.
ex.az:
1. 错误：把外键画成 Product 的属性。
  2. 删掉该椭圆。
  3. 画菱形 Sell 连 Store 和 Product。

ex.q: LETTER(LID, RADD, PID, MID). Which ellipses does Letter have in the ER diagram?
ex.a:
1. PID and MID are foreign keys → not ellipses.
  2. Letter has only Letter ID (underlined) and Recipient address.
  3. Links: Postman ◇Deliver◇ Letter, Letter ◇Originate from◇ Mailbox.
ex.az:
1. PID、MID 是外键，不画。
  2. 只有 Letter ID 和 Recipient address。

ex.q: Tables BOOK(<u>BID</u>, TITLE, PUBID) and PUBLISHER(<u>PUBID</u>, PNAME). Draw the ER diagram in words.
ex.a:
1. Rectangles: Book, Publisher.
  2. Book ellipses: Book ID, Title. (PUBID is a FK → not drawn on Book.)
  3. Publisher ellipses: Publisher ID, Publisher name.
  4. Diamond Publish: Publisher 1 — M Book (FK is on the many side, BOOK).
ex.az:
1. 两个长方形。
  2. Book 只画 Book ID、Title。
  3. 菱形 Publish，Publisher 1 对 M Book。

demo.title: Turning a foreign key into a relationship

frames.en: LETTER(LID, RADD, PID, MID). PID and MID point to other tables.
Letter keeps only <u>Letter ID</u> and Recipient address as ellipses.
PID → diamond Deliver to Postman; MID → diamond Originate from to Mailbox.

cards.en:
Intuition: must every student join a sports event? Yes → must. May a student skip it? → may. That "must or may" is the participation constraint.

The rule: the participation constraint of a relationship says whether each entity of an entity type takes part in the relationship. Each relationship has two sides; each side is mandatory or optional, shown by a symbol on the line.

Symbol on the line, next to entity BSideMeaning
short bar |Mandatory sideeach A must be linked to at least one B
circle OOptional sideeach A may or may not be linked to a B

Careful (book's way): the symbol is drawn next to the entity being counted. "A student must join a sports event" → the bar | is drawn next to Sports event (Student ◇Join◇ |Sports event). We say "the right side is mandatory".

Exam wording: "The participation constraint specifies whether each entity of an entity type participates in a relationship or not." "Since each student must join a sports event, the right side is mandatory."
cards.zh:
直觉：每个学生都必须参加运动项目吗？必须 → must；可参加可不参加 → may。这就是参与限制。

规则：每个关系有两面（two sides），每面是 mandatory 或 optional，用线上的符号表示。

画在 B 旁边的符号Side意思
短竖线 |Mandatory side每个 A 必须连到至少一个 B
圆圈 OOptional side每个 A 可以有也可以没有 B

注意（课本画法）：符号画在被数的那个实体旁边。“A student must join a sports event” → 竖线画在 Sports event 旁边，称为 “the right side is mandatory”。

考试写法："The participation constraint specifies whether each entity of an entity type participates in a relationship or not." "Since each student must join a sports event, the right side is mandatory."

ex.q: Student ◇Join◇ Sports event. "Every student must join a sports event; some events may have no students." State each side.
ex.a:
1. 'Each student must join an event' counts events per student → symbol next to Sports event → right side mandatory (|).
  2. 'An event may have no students' counts students per event → symbol next to Student → left side optional (O).
ex.az:
1. 每个学生必须参加 → 右面（Sports event 旁）强制 |。
  2. 项目可以没有学生 → 左面（Student 旁）非强制 O。

ex.q: Textbook Example 5.2(a): Computer ◇Be assigned to◇ Student (Computer drawn on the left). 40 computers, 25 students, each student is assigned exactly one computer.
ex.a:
1. 'Each student is assigned one computer' counts computers per student → symbol next to Computer → left side mandatory.
  2. More computers than students, so some computers have no student → symbol next to Student → right side optional.
ex.az:
1. 每个学生必有一台电脑 → Computer 旁（左面）强制。
  2. 电脑多于学生，有些电脑没人用 → Student 旁（右面）非强制。

ex.q: A student draws the bar | next to Student for "each student must join an event".
ex.a:
1. Mistake: putting the symbol next to the entity in the subject of the sentence.
  2. The sentence tells us how many events each student has, so the symbol goes next to Sports event.
  3. Tip: "Each A must/may ... B" → symbol next to B.
ex.az:
1. 错误：把符号画在主语实体旁。
  2. 句子说的是每个学生有几个项目，所以画在 Sports event 旁。
  3. 口诀：“Each A must/may ... B” → 符号画在 B 旁。

frames.en: "Each student must join a sports event." It tells us how many events one student has.
frames.zh: 这句话说的是每个学生有几个项目。

frames.en: Put the mandatory bar | next to Sports event: right side mandatory.
frames.zh: 竖线画在 Sports event 旁：右面强制。

frames.en: "An event may have no students" → circle O next to Student: left side optional.
frames.zh: 圆圈 O 画在 Student 旁：左面非强制。

cards.t: Mandatory and optional sides in real life
cards.tz: 生活中的强制与非强制
cards.en:
Intuition: turn every rule into the pattern "Each A must / may ... B". "must" → mandatory, "may or may not" → optional, and the symbol goes next to B.

Mandatory side examples (from the book):

  • Each employee must belong to one department.
  • Every course must be taught by one or more lecturers.
  • Each vehicle must have a registration plate.

Optional side examples:

  • An employee may or may not have tasks at hand.
  • Each hotel room may or may not be occupied by guests.
  • A citizen may or may not own a vehicle.

Decide from the scenario's words, not your opinion.

Exam wording: "Each employee must belong to one department, so the side next to Department is mandatory."
cards.zh:
直觉：把规则改写成 “Each A must / may ... B”：must → mandatory，may or may not → optional，符号画在 B 旁。

强制例子：每个员工必须属于一个部门；每个课程必须由一位或以上讲师教；每辆车必须有车牌。

非强制例子：员工可以有也可以没有手头任务；酒店房间可能空着；市民可以没有车。

按题目文字判断，不按个人看法。

考试写法："Each employee must belong to one department, so the side next to Department is mandatory."

ex.q: Employee ◇Belong to◇ Department. Each employee must belong to one department; a new department may have no staff yet.
ex.a:
1. 'Each employee must ... department' → bar | next to Department (mandatory).
  2. 'A department may have no staff' → circle O next to Employee (optional).

ex.q: Citizen ◇Own◇ Vehicle. A citizen may or may not own a vehicle; each vehicle must be owned by a citizen.
ex.a:
1. 'Citizen may or may not own a vehicle' → O next to Vehicle.
  2. 'Each vehicle must be owned by a citizen' → | next to Citizen.

ex.q: Hotel: Room ◇Be occupied by◇ Guest. A student says "rooms are for guests, so it is mandatory".
ex.a:
1. Mistake: using purpose instead of the rule.
  2. A room may or may not be occupied at a given time → the side next to Guest is optional.
ex.az:
1. 错误：用用途判断。
  2. 房间可以空着 → Guest 旁非强制。

frames.en: "A department may have no staff yet."
"Each department may have no employee." A = Department, B = Employee.
Circle O next to Employee.

cards.en:
Intuition: a school and its principal: every school must have a principal, and every principal must belong to a school.

The rule: both sides mandatory (bar | on both ends). For each entity a there must be at least one related b, and vice versa.

Database effect: no entity on either side can be left unlinked; foreign keys are NOT NULL.

Exam wording: "For each school there must be a principal, and each principal must belong to a school, so both sides are mandatory."
cards.zh:
直觉：学校与校长：每间学校必须有校长，每位校长必须属于一间学校。

规则：两面都强制（两端都是 |）：每个 a 至少有一个 b，反之亦然。

数据库影响：两边都不能落单，外键 NOT NULL。

考试写法："For each school there must be a principal, and each principal must belong to a school, so both sides are mandatory."

ex.q: Textbook Example 5.2(c): Student ◇Belong to◇ Class. Every student belongs to a class; each class has about 20–30 students.
ex.a:
1. Every student belongs to a class → | next to Class.
  2. Each class has 20–30 (≥1) students → | next to Student.
  3. Both mandatory.
ex.az: 1. 两边都强制（每班 20–30 人即至少 1 人）。

ex.q: Order ◇Contain◇ Order line. Every order has at least one line; every line belongs to one order.
ex.a:
1. | next to Order line.
  2. | next to Order.
  3. Case A.

ex.q: Teacher ◇Be assigned to◇ Class (class teacher). A student says both sides are mandatory.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: each class must have a class teacher, but a teacher may or may not be a class teacher.
  2. So it is case B: | next to Teacher, O next to Class.
ex.az:
1. 错误：老师不一定是班主任。
  2. 应为情况 B。

demo.query: SELECT SCHNAME, PNAME FROM SCHOOL s JOIN PRINCIPAL p ON s.SCHID = p.SCHID;
demo.note: Every school appears with a principal and every principal has a school (SCHID NOT NULL): both sides mandatory.

cards.tz: B. 一边强制一边非强制
cards.en:
Intuition: teachers and classes: each class must have a class teacher, but a teacher may or may not be a class teacher.

The rule: if the side of A is mandatory and that of B is optional:

  • for each b, there must be at least one related a;
  • for each a, there may or may not be a related b.

This is the most common case.

Exam wording: "Each class must have a class teacher, so the side next to Teacher is mandatory; a teacher may or may not be a class teacher, so the side next to Class is optional."
cards.zh:
直觉：每个班必须有班主任，但老师不一定是班主任。

规则：A 面强制、B 面非强制：每个 b 必须有相关 a；每个 a 可有可无 b。最常见。

考试写法："Each class must have a class teacher, so the side next to Teacher is mandatory; a teacher may or may not be a class teacher, so the side next to Class is optional."

ex.q: Member ◇Borrow◇ Loan record. Each loan must be made by a member; a member may have no loans.
ex.a:
1. | next to Member.
  2. O next to Loan.
  3. Case B.

ex.q: Textbook Example 5.2(d): Award ◇Be given to◇ Student. 16 subjects × 3 awards = 48 awards, 40 students, ≥5 students per subject.
ex.a:
1. Students are not guaranteed an award → the side next to Award is optional.
  2. Each subject has ≥3 students, so every award has a recipient → the side next to Student is mandatory.
ex.az:
1. 学生不一定得奖 → Award 旁非强制。
  2. 每个奖一定有人得 → Student 旁强制。

ex.q: 48 awards > 40 students, so a student concludes every student must get an award.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: more awards than students does not guarantee each student one; one top student could win many.
  2. Follow the description: students are not guaranteed an award → optional.
ex.az:
1. 错误：奖多于人不代表人人有奖。
  2. 按描述 → 非强制。

demo.query: SELECT t.TNAME, c.CLASSNAME FROM TEACHER t LEFT JOIN CLASS c ON t.TID = c.TID;
demo.note: Every class has a teacher (TID NOT NULL). Ms Ho has no class (NULL): the class side is optional.

cards.en:
Intuition: citizens and diseases: a citizen may or may not have a disease, and a disease may or may not have an infected citizen.

The rule: both sides optional (circle O on both ends). For each a there may or may not be a related b, and vice versa.

Database effect: records on both sides can exist alone; a link table may have no rows for some of them.

Exam wording: "Each citizen may or may not be infected with a disease and each disease may or may not infect a citizen, so both sides are optional."
cards.zh:
直觉：市民与疾病：市民可能没病；某疾病可能没人感染。

规则：两面都非强制（两端都是 O）。

数据库影响：两边记录都可单独存在。

考试写法："Each citizen may or may not be infected with a disease and each disease may or may not infect a citizen, so both sides are optional."

ex.q: Textbook Example 5.2(b): Student ◇Borrow◇ Book.
ex.a:
1. A book is not guaranteed to be borrowed → optional.
  2. Students may choose not to borrow → optional.
  3. Case C.

ex.q: Student ◇Join◇ Club. A student may join no club; a new club may have no members.
ex.a:
1. O next to Club.
  2. O next to Student.

ex.q: A student says optional–optional means the relationship can be deleted from the design.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: optional only means 'not every entity takes part'.
  2. Many students still join clubs, so the links must be stored.

demo.query: SELECT c.CNAME, COUNT(m.SID) AS MEMBERS FROM CLUB c LEFT JOIN MEMBERSHIP m ON c.CID = m.CID GROUP BY c.CID;
demo.note: Drama has 0 members, and Cat is in no club: both sides optional.

cards.en:
Method:

  1. Find the two entity types and the relationship verb.
  2. Rewrite each rule as "Each A must/may ... B".
  3. Keyword → side type (table below).
  4. Draw the symbol next to B. Write a full sentence as your reason.
KeywordSide
must, every ... at least one, always, exactly onemandatory |
may or may not, not guaranteed, can choose not to, some ... neveroptional O

Hidden clues: "about 20 to 30 students per class" means at least one → mandatory. "More computers than students" means some computers unused → optional.

Exam wording: "Since each [A] must [verb] [B], the side next to [B] is mandatory."
cards.zh:
方法：

  1. 找两个实体和关系动词。
  2. 每条规则改写成 “Each A must/may ... B”。
  3. 按关键词判断。
  4. 符号画在 B 旁，写完整句子作理由。
关键词Side
must / every ... at least one / always / exactly onemandatory |
may or may not / not guaranteed / can choose not tooptional O

隐藏线索：“每班约 20–30 人”= 至少一人 → 强制；“电脑比学生多”= 有电脑没人用 → 非强制。

考试写法："Since each [A] must [verb] [B], the side next to [B] is mandatory."

ex.q: "Each flight must be operated by one aircraft. An aircraft may be under repair and operate no flight." (Flight ◇Be operated by◇ Aircraft)
ex.a:
1. Each flight must ... aircraft → | next to Aircraft.
  2. Each aircraft may ... no flight → O next to Flight.

ex.q: "Each company may own zero or any number of offices. Each office is owned by one company." (textbook)
ex.a:
1. Company may own zero offices → right side (Office) optional.
  2. Each office owned by one company → left side (Company) mandatory.

ex.q: "Each patient must see a doctor." A student marks both sides mandatory.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: this sentence only gives the side next to Doctor (mandatory).
  2. The side next to Patient needs another clue, e.g. "a new doctor may have no patients" → optional. If none is given, state your assumption.
ex.az:
1. 错误：一句话只决定一面。
  2. 另一面要找线索或写假设。

frames.en: "Each company may own zero offices." A=Company, B=Office.
frames.zh: 每间公司可以没有办公室。

frames.en: O next to Office (right side optional).
"Each office is owned by one company" → | next to Company.

cards.en:
Intuition: participation asks "at least one?"; cardinality asks "at most how many?" One or many?

The rule: the cardinality of a relationship specifies how many entities of one entity type can be related to entities of another entity type. It is written as a character beside the line:

Character next to BMeaning
1each A relates to one B at most
M (or N)each A can relate to many B

Like the participation symbol, it is written next to the entity being counted: "A student may join many sports events" → M next to Sports event.

Three types: one-to-one (1:1), one-to-many (1:M), many-to-many (M:N).

Exam wording: "The cardinality specifies how many entities of an entity type can be related to entities of another entity type."
cards.zh:
直觉：参与限制问“至少一个吗？”；cardinality 问“最多几个？”一个还是多个。

规则：基数说明一个实体类型的实体能与另一实体类型的多少个实体相关，用线旁的字符表示：1＝最多一个；M/N＝可以多个。

和参与符号一样，写在被数的实体旁边：“A student may join many sports events” → M 写在 Sports event 旁。

三种：1:1、1:M、M:N。

考试写法："The cardinality specifies how many entities of an entity type can be related to entities of another entity type."

ex.q: "Each department has one department head only; each head leads one department." Cardinality?
ex.a:
1. Each department → 1 head: write 1 next to Head.
  2. Each head → 1 department: write 1 next to Department.
  3. One-to-one.

ex.q: "A school has multiple classrooms; each classroom belongs to one school."
ex.a:
1. School → many classrooms: M next to Classroom.
  2. Classroom → one school: 1 next to School.
  3. School 1 — Have — M Classroom: one-to-many.
ex.az: 1. Classroom 旁 M，School 旁 1 → 一对多。

ex.q: "Each student joins one sports event." A student writes 1 next to Student.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: the character goes next to the entity being counted.
  2. The sentence counts events per student → write 1 next to Sports event.
ex.az:
1. 错误：字符写在被数的实体旁。
  2. 应写在 Sports event 旁。

demo.query: SELECT s.NAME, COUNT(e.EID) AS SUBJECTS FROM STUDENT s LEFT JOIN ENROLMENT e ON s.SID = e.SID GROUP BY s.SID;
demo.note: Counting how many electives each student is related to: Clem has 3, so the cardinality next to Elective is 'many'.

cards.tz: 参与限制 vs 基数
cards.en:
Intuition: a lift sign says "minimum 1 person to run, maximum 10 people". Participation = minimum, cardinality = maximum.

Participation constraintCardinality
Questionmust there be at least one?at most one or many?
Symbolbar | or circle O1 or M/N

Together at one end:

ParticipationCardinalityMeaning
Mandatory1exactly one
Optional1zero or one
MandatoryMat least one, if not many
OptionalMzero or many

Exam wording: describe both: "Each publisher publishes one or more books, while each book is published by exactly one publisher."
cards.zh:
直觉：电梯：“最少 1 人才开，最多 10 人”。参与限制＝最少，基数＝最多。

参与基数意思
强制1恰好一个
非强制1零或一个
强制M一个或以上
非强制M零或多个

考试写法：两者都要描述："Each publisher publishes one or more books, while each book is published by exactly one publisher."

ex.q: Translate: next to Office: optional + M (Company ◇Own◇ Office).
ex.a:
1. Optional = minimum 0; M = maximum many.
  2. "Each company owns zero or many offices."
ex.az: 1. 每间公司拥有零或多个办公室。

ex.q: "Each worker must work in only one office." What goes next to Office?
ex.a:
1. 'must' → mandatory |.
  2. 'only one' → 1.
  3. Next to Office: | and 1 = exactly one.

ex.q: A student writes "M means at least one".
ex.a:
1. Mistake: mixing min and max.
  2. M only says the maximum is many. Whether the minimum is 0 or 1 comes from the participation symbol.
ex.az: 1. 错误：M 只说最多多个，最少由参与符号决定。

demo.title: Reading one end of a line

frames.en: Circle O next to Office → minimum 0.
M next to Office → maximum many.
"Each company owns zero or many offices."

cards.en:
Intuition: one school, one principal.

The rule: in a one-to-one (1:1) relationship, for each entity a there is at most one related b, and vice versa. Write 1 on both ends.

How to store it: put the primary key of one table into the other as a foreign key. If one side is optional, put the FK where most rows will have a value, or allow NULL. Book example: TEACHER(TID, TNAME, SEX, TENURE, CID) – a teacher who is not a class teacher has CID = NULL.

Exam wording: "For each school there is exactly one principal, and each principal belongs to exactly one school, so it is a one-to-one relationship."
cards.zh:
直觉：一间学校一个校长。

规则：1:1：每个 a 最多一个 b，反之亦然，两端都写 1。

存法：把一个表的主键放进另一个表做外键。若一边非强制，可允许 NULL。课本例：TEACHER(TID, ..., CID)，不是班主任的老师 CID 为 NULL。

考试写法："For each school there is exactly one principal, and each principal belongs to exactly one school, so it is a one-to-one relationship."

ex.q: SCHOOL(<u>SID</u>, SNAME, DISTRICT, PID) and PRINCIPAL(<u>PID</u>, PNAME, TENURE). What is the relationship and where is the FK?
ex.a:
1. One school ↔ one principal → 1:1.
  2. FK: SCHOOL.PID references PRINCIPAL.PID.
  3. ER: School 1 — Have — 1 Principal.

ex.q: Employee ↔ Desk: each employee has exactly one desk; a desk holds one employee at a time. Give the cardinality.
ex.a:
1. 1 next to Desk, 1 next to Employee.
  2. One-to-one.

ex.q: Teacher 1 — Be assigned to — 1 Class. A student puts TID in CLASS and also CID in TEACHER.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: storing the link twice. The two copies can disagree (Class 3A says Adam, Adam says 3B).
  2. One FK is enough: e.g. CID in TEACHER (NULL if not a class teacher).
ex.az:
1. 错误：两边都放外键，可能不一致。
  2. 只放一边即可。

demo.query: SELECT t.TNAME, c.CNAME, c.ROOM FROM TEACHER t LEFT JOIN CLASS c ON t.CID = c.CID;
demo.note: Textbook data (Table 5.8). UNIQUE CID keeps it one-to-one; Ella and Bea are not class teachers (NULL).

cards.t: Merging a one-to-one relationship into an attribute
cards.en:
Intuition: if all you need about the principal is a name, you don't need a whole table for principals. Just write the name on the school's record.

The rule: in a 1:1 relationship, if we are NOT interested in storing any extra data about the other entity, it can become an attribute: SCHOOL(SID, SNAME, DISTRICT, PRINCIPAL). Principal is no longer an entity type.

Trade-off: simplicity and performance (no join) vs flexibility and level of detail (cannot store the principal's tenure, phone...). Proceed with caution.

Only for 1:1. For 1:M, merging would repeat data.

Exam wording: "This approach trades flexibility and the level of details for simplicity and performance."
cards.zh:
直觉：如果只需要校长名字，就不必为校长建一个表，直接写在学校记录里。

规则：1:1 中若不需存对方的其他数据，可把它变成属性：SCHOOL(SID, SNAME, DISTRICT, PRINCIPAL)。

取舍：换来简单和性能（免 join），失去灵活性和细节。要谨慎。只适用 1:1。

考试写法："This approach trades flexibility and the level of details for simplicity and performance."

ex.q: Write the merged schema for School 1—Have—1 Principal if only the name is needed.
ex.a:
1. Remove table PRINCIPAL.
  2. Add field PRINCIPAL to SCHOOL.
  3. SCHOOL(SID, SNAME, DISTRICT, PRINCIPAL).

ex.q: Later the school wants to store the principal's tenure. What happens?
ex.a:
1. The table structure must change: add TENURE to SCHOOL, or split Principal out again.
  2. This is the lost flexibility.
ex.az: 1. 要改表结构 → 失去灵活性。

ex.q: Class 1—Have—M Student. A student merges students into CLASS as STUDENTS='Ada, Clem, Eva'.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: merging only works for 1:1.
  2. For 1:M, one field would hold many values (breaks 1NF) and is hard to search.
  3. Keep two tables with CID as FK in STUDENT.
ex.az:
1. 错误：只适用一对一。
  2. 一对多合并会一格多值。

notes.t: One table only: the principal's name is a normal field.
notes.tz: 只有一个表，校长名是普通字段。

notes.t: Insert a school with its principal's name.
Another school.
No join needed to get the principal: faster and simpler.
notes.tz: 无需 join 即可取得校长名。

cards.en:
Intuition: one class has many students, but each student is in only one class.

The rule: in a one-to-many (1:M) relationship, each a can relate to many b, and each b relates to at most one a. ER: Class 1 — Have — M Student.

How to store it: put the primary key of the "one" side into the "many" side as a foreign key: STUDENT(SID, NAME, SEX, CID). The FK always goes on the many side.

Swap the order and it reads "many-to-one" – same thing.

Exam wording: "Each class has at least one, if not many, students, and each student belongs to exactly one class. The primary key of CLASS is stored in STUDENT as a foreign key."
cards.zh:
直觉：一个班多个学生，每个学生只在一个班。

规则：1:M：每个 a 可对多个 b，每个 b 最多一个 a。ER：Class 1 — Have — M Student。

存法：把“一”方主键放进“多”方做外键：STUDENT(SID, NAME, SEX, CID)。外键永远放在 many 一方。

考试写法："Each class has at least one, if not many, students, and each student belongs to exactly one class. The primary key of CLASS is stored in STUDENT as a foreign key."

ex.q: Citizen ◇Have◇ Criminal record: a citizen may have many records or none; each record belongs to exactly one citizen. Draw and store it.
ex.a:
1. M next to Criminal record (optional O); 1 next to Citizen (mandatory |).
  2. FK on the many side: CRIMINALRECORD(RID, CRIME, DATE, CID).
ex.az:
1. Citizen 1 — M Record。
  2. 外键 CID 放在 CRIMINALRECORD。

ex.q: Account ◇Place◇ Food order. Where is the FK?
ex.a:
1. An account places many orders; an order comes from one account → 1:M.
  2. FK: FOODORDER.AID.

ex.q: A student stores Class 1:M Student by putting SID in CLASS.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: a class has many students, so CLASS would need many SID values in one field (or many rows repeating the class).
  2. Right: CID in STUDENT (each student has exactly one CID).
ex.az:
1. 错误：外键放错在 one 一方。
  2. 应把 CID 放在 STUDENT。

demo.query: SELECT c.CNAME, s.NAME FROM CLASS c JOIN STUDENT s ON c.CID = s.CID ORDER BY c.CNAME;
demo.note: Textbook Table 5.9. CID (FK) sits in STUDENT, the many side. 3B appears with 3 students.

cards.t: Do not store a one-to-many relationship in one table
cards.tz: 一对多不要合成一个表
cards.en:
Intuition: if you write the class room number on every student card, changing the room means rewriting many cards.

The rule: storing two entity types with a 1:M relationship in one table causes redundant data. STUDENT(SID, NAME, SEX, CNAME, ROOM): room 402 for class 3B is stored 3 times.

  • Change 3B's room 402 → 403: three records must be updated (else inconsistent).
  • Delete Ada: the room of class 3A is lost.

These problems are called anomalies (5.4) and are fixed by normalisation (5.5).

Exam wording: "Storing them in a single table results in redundant data, which may lead to data inconsistency."
cards.zh:
直觉：每张学生卡都写班房号，换房就要改很多张。

规则：把 1:M 两个实体放一个表会产生冗余：3B 的房号 402 存 3 次。

  • 改房号要改 3 条，漏改就不一致。
  • 删除 Ada，3A 的房号就消失。

这些叫 anomalies（5.4），用 normalisation 解决（5.5）。

考试写法："Storing them in a single table results in redundant data, which may lead to data inconsistency."

ex.q: How many records change if 3B moves to room 403 (merged table, 3 students in 3B)? And in the two-table design?
ex.a:
1. Merged: 3 records (Clem, Eva, Finn).
  2. Two tables: 1 record in CLASS.
ex.az: 1. 合表改 3 条，分表改 1 条。

ex.q: What is lost if Gabe (only student in 3C) is deleted from the merged table?
ex.a:
1. The only record with 3C disappears.
  2. Room 203 of 3C is lost.

ex.q: A student updates only Clem's row to 403 and says the job is done.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: Eva and Finn still show 402.
  2. 3B now has two rooms → inconsistent.
  3. Use UPDATE ... WHERE CNAME='3B', or better, normalise.

demo.query: SELECT CNAME, ROOM, COUNT(*) AS N FROM STUDENT GROUP BY CNAME, ROOM;
demo.note: Only Clem's row was updated: class 3B now has two different rooms (402 and 403).

cards.en:
Intuition: a student takes many electives; an elective has many students.

The rule: in a many-to-many (M:N) relationship, each a can relate to many b and vice versa. Write M on one end and N on the other: Student M — Enrol in — N Elective subject.

How to store it: you cannot put one FK in either table. Create a separate table (e.g. ENROLMENT(SID, EID)), one record per pair.

Exam wording: "Each student enrols in one or more elective subjects and each subject is enrolled in by one or more students. A separate table is created to represent the many-to-many relationship."
cards.zh:
直觉：一个学生选多科，一科有多个学生。

规则：M:N：每个 a 可对多个 b，反之亦然。一端 M，另一端 N。

存法：不能只在一边放外键，要建独立的表（如 ENROLMENT(SID, EID)），每对一条记录。

考试写法："... A separate table is created to represent the many-to-many relationship."

ex.q: Citizen ◇Own◇ Property: a citizen may own many properties or none; a property may be owned by many citizens or none. Draw it.
ex.a:
1. M next to Property, N next to Citizen.
  2. Both ends optional (O).
  3. Store with OWNERSHIP(CID, PID).

ex.q: Book and Author: a book has one or more authors; an author writes one or more books.
ex.a:
1. Both ends mandatory, M and N.
  2. Table WRITE(ISBN, AID).

ex.q: A student writes Student M — Enrol in — M Elective.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: in a many-to-many relationship one character is usually changed to N.
  2. Write Student M — Enrol in — N Elective subject.

demo.query: SELECT s.NAME, e.ENAME FROM STUDENT s JOIN ENROLMENT n ON s.SID = n.SID JOIN ELECTIVE e ON n.EID = e.EID ORDER BY s.NAME;
demo.note: Textbook Table 5.11: ENROLMENT stores one row per student–subject pair. Clem has 3 subjects; Physics has 3 students.

cards.t: Drawing an ER diagram from a scenario
cards.en:
Method: one sentence at a time.

  1. Nouns → entity types (rectangles). Verb → relationship (diamond).
  2. must / may → participation (| or O).
  3. one, only one, exclusively → 1; many, multiple, any number, several → M.
  4. Both ends many → write M and N.
  5. Put each symbol next to the entity being counted.
  6. Add ellipses and underline keys.

Exam wording: for each end, write: "The right side of this relationship is optional and its cardinality is many." (the book's style)
cards.zh:
方法：一句一句处理。

  1. 名词 → 实体；动词 → 关系。
  2. must/may → 参与。
  3. one/only one/exclusively → 1；many/multiple/any number → M。
  4. 两端都多 → M 和 N。
  5. 符号写在被数的实体旁。
  6. 加属性、主键下划线。

考试写法："The right side of this relationship is optional and its cardinality is many."

ex.q: Textbook Example 5.3(a): "Each company may own zero or any number of offices. Each office is exclusively owned by one company. Every worker must work in only one office. There are always many workers in an office."
ex.a:
1. Company—Own—Office: right side optional, M; left side mandatory, 1.
  2. Office—Have—Worker: left side (Office) mandatory, 1; right side (Worker) mandatory, M.
  3. Result: Company 1 — Own — M Office 1 — Have — M Worker.
ex.az:
1. Company 1—Own—M Office（Office 旁 O）。
  2. Office 1—Have—M Worker（两边强制）。

ex.q: Textbook Example 5.3(b): "Each menu offers multiple dishes. A dish must appear on one or more menus. A customer orders at least one dish. Some dishes are ordered by many customers, some never."
ex.a:
1. Menu M — Offer — N Dish, both mandatory.
  2. Dish M — Be ordered by — N Customer: left side (next to Dish) mandatory; right side (next to Customer) optional.
ex.az:
1. Menu M—N Dish，两边强制。
  2. Dish M—N Customer，Customer 旁非强制。

ex.q: "A school has multiple classrooms." A student draws School M — Have — 1 Classroom.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: M placed next to the wrong entity.
  2. 'Multiple classrooms per school' → M next to Classroom: School 1 — Have — M Classroom.
ex.az:
1. 错误：M 放错位置。
  2. 应为 School 1 — M Classroom。

frames.en: "Each company may own zero or any number of offices." → next to Office: O and M.
"Each office is exclusively owned by one company." → next to Company: | and 1.
Worker must work in only one office → next to Office: | 1. Always many workers → next to Worker: | M.

cards.t: From table structure to ER diagram
cards.tz: 由表结构反推 ER 图
cards.en:
Intuition: the foreign keys are footprints that show where the relationships are.

Rules:

  • Each table → a rectangle; its non-FK fields → ellipses.
  • A FK in X referencing Y → a diamond between X and Y. X is the many side: M next to X, 1 next to Y.
  • FK NOT NULL → each X must have a Y → | next to Y. FK may be NULL → O next to Y.
  • Nothing forces every Y to appear in X → usually O next to X.
  • A table whose key is two FKs = resolved M:N.

Exam wording: "Since PID in LETTER is a foreign key and NOT NULL, each letter is delivered by exactly one postman, while a postman may deliver many letters."
cards.zh:
直觉：外键就是关系留下的脚印。

  • 每个表 → 长方形；非外键字段 → 椭圆。
  • X 中外键指向 Y → X、Y 间画菱形，X 是 many（X 旁 M，Y 旁 1）。
  • 外键 NOT NULL → Y 旁 |；可 NULL → Y 旁 O。
  • 通常 X 旁是 O。
  • 主键由两个外键组成的表 = 已拆开的 M:N。

考试写法："Since PID in LETTER is a foreign key and NOT NULL, each letter is delivered by exactly one postman, while a postman may deliver many letters."

ex.q: Textbook Example 5.3 Q2: POSTMAN(<u>PID</u>, PNAME, SEX), LETTER(<u>LID</u>, RADD, PID NOT NULL, MID NOT NULL), MAILBOX(<u>MID</u>, ...). Draw the ER diagram.
ex.a:
1. Rectangles Postman, Letter, Mailbox. Letter ellipses: Letter ID, Recipient address only.
  2. Postman 1 — Deliver — M Letter; | next to Postman (NOT NULL), O next to Letter.
  3. Letter M — Originate from — 1 Mailbox; | next to Mailbox, O next to Letter.
ex.az:
1. 三个长方形。
  2. Postman 1—Deliver—M Letter。
  3. Letter M—Originate from—1 Mailbox。

ex.q: OWNERSHIP(<u>CID, PID</u>) with CID → CITIZEN, PID → PROPERTY. What does it represent?
ex.a:
1. Primary key made of two FKs.
  2. It is a resolved many-to-many: Citizen M — Own — N Property.
ex.az: 1. 两个外键组成主键 → 多对多。

ex.q: A student sees LETTER.PID and draws Letter 1 — Deliver — M Postman.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: the table holding the FK is the many side.
  2. Many letters share one PID → Postman 1 — Deliver — M Letter.
ex.az: 1. 错误：有外键的表是 many 一方。

demo.query: SELECT p.PNAME, COUNT(l.LID) AS LETTERS FROM POSTMAN p LEFT JOIN LETTER l ON p.PID = l.PID GROUP BY p.PID;
demo.note: PID repeats in LETTER (Ken: 2 letters) → Letter is the many side. Joe has 0 letters → optional next to Letter.

cards.t: Activity 5.1: four ways to store a many-to-many relationship
cards.en:
Intuition: there are many ways to record "who takes which elective". Only one survives all real tasks.

MethodProblem
1. One field holds a list: EIDLIST = '1,11,12'Multiple values in one field. LIKE '%1%' also matches 11 and 12; can't JOIN or COUNT easily.
2. One Yes/No field per subject: HISTORY, PHYSICS, ICTRepeating attributes. New subject → new field; can't join to get rooms.
3. ELEC1, ELEC2, ELEC3Repeating attributes. 4th subject → new field; long OR queries; many NULLs.
4. Separate table ENROLMENT(SID, EID)Best: normal JOIN, WHERE, COUNT; structure never changes.

Methods 1–3 break 1NF.

Exam wording: "A separate table with one record for each student–subject pair avoids multiple values in a field and repeating attributes."
cards.zh:
直觉：“谁选了哪科”有很多存法，只有一种能应付所有任务。

方法问题
1. 一个字段存列表一格多值；LIKE '%1%' 会误中 11、12。
2. 每科一个是/否字段重复属性，新科要加字段。
3. ELEC1–3重复属性，第 4 科要加字段；查询长，多 NULL。
4. 独立表 ENROLMENT最好。

方法 1–3 违反 1NF。

考试写法："A separate table with one record for each student–subject pair avoids multiple values in a field and repeating attributes."

ex.q: With Method 4, list students enrolled in History (EID 1).
ex.a:
1. Join STUDENT and ENROLMENT on SID.
  2. Filter EID = 1.
  3. See code: returns Clem, Eva.

ex.q: With Method 3, how would you find History students, and why is it bad?
ex.a:
1. WHERE ELEC1=1 OR ELEC2=1 OR ELEC3=1.
  2. Every query needs 3 conditions; adding ELEC4 means changing the table and every query.
ex.az: 1. 要三个 OR；加科就要改表和查询。

ex.q: With Method 1, a student uses WHERE EIDLIST LIKE '%1%' to find History students.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: '%1%' matches any list containing the digit 1, e.g. '11' (Physics) and '12' (ICT).
  2. The demo shows Ada and Finn wrongly returned.
  3. Fix: use Method 4 and WHERE EID = 1.

notes.t: Show the student's name.
Use two tables with aliases s and e.
Join on SID and keep only History (EID 1).
notes.tz: 按 SID 连接并只要 EID=1。

demo.setup:
CREATE TABLE S1(SID TEXT, NAME TEXT, EIDLIST TEXT);
INSERT INTO S1 VALUES('03493','Ada','11'),('03496','Clem','1,11,12'),('03505','Eva','1'),('03510','Finn','12');
demo.query: SELECT NAME, EIDLIST FROM S1 WHERE EIDLIST LIKE '%1%';
demo.note: Method 1 bug: only Clem and Eva take History (1), but Ada (11) and Finn (12) are also returned.

cards.en:
Intuition: a many-to-many link is like a tangle of strings. Put a "knot table" in the middle so each string goes only one way.

The rule: to resolve a M:N relationship, add an associative entity type in the middle. M:N becomes 1:M + M:1.

Student M — Enrol in — N Elective → Student 1 — Make — M Enrolment M — Be made for — 1 Elective.

The new table ENROLMENT(SID, EID) has two foreign keys; together they form a composite primary key, so the same pair cannot be stored twice.

Other examples: Citizen–Ownership–Property; Actor–Role–Movie; Doctor–Treatment–Patient; Customer–Order–Product.

Exam wording: "The many-to-many relationship is resolved into two one-to-many relationships by adding an associative entity type, whose table contains the primary keys of both tables as foreign keys."
cards.zh:
直觉：多对多像一团乱线，中间加一个“结”（关联表），让每条线只走一个方向。

规则：加 associative entity type，M:N 变成 1:M + M:1。

新表 ENROLMENT(SID, EID) 有两个外键，合起来做复合主键，同一对不能重复。

其他例：Ownership、Role、Treatment、Order。

考试写法："The many-to-many relationship is resolved into two one-to-many relationships by adding an associative entity type..."

ex.q: Resolve Doctor M — Treat — N Patient.
ex.a:
1. Add entity Treatment.
  2. Doctor 1 — Provide — M Treatment M — Be given to — 1 Patient.
  3. TREATMENT(DID, PID, TDATE, TNAME).
ex.az: 1. 加 Treatment 实体，拆成两个一对多。

ex.q: How many tables are needed for Actor M — Star in — N Movie?
ex.a:
1. ACTOR, MOVIE, plus associative ROLE.
  2. 3 tables.

ex.q: A student makes ENROLMENT's primary key SID only.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: a student has many enrolments, so SID repeats → can't be the key.
  2. Use the composite key (SID, EID). The demo shows the duplicate pair is rejected.
ex.az:
1. 错误：SID 会重复，不能单独做主键。
  2. 用 (SID, EID)。

notes.t: Create the associative table.
SID: links to a student.
EID: links to an elective.
Composite primary key: the pair must be unique.
SID is a foreign key to STUDENT.
EID is a foreign key to ELECTIVE.
End of definition.
Clem takes History and Physics: two rows, same SID.
notes.tz: Clem 两科，SID 重复两次。

notes.t: Show the rows.

code.in: CREATE TABLE STUDENT(SID CHAR(5) PRIMARY KEY); CREATE TABLE ELECTIVE(EID INT PRIMARY KEY);

frames.en: Student M — Enrol in — N Elective. No single FK can store this.
frames.zh: 多对多，单个外键存不了。

frames.en: Replace the diamond with a new entity Enrolment.
frames.zh: 把菱形换成新实体 Enrolment。

frames.en: ENROLMENT(<u>SID, EID</u>): two FKs = composite PK. Rows: (03496,1), (03496,11), (03496,12)...
frames.zh: ENROLMENT 两个外键做复合主键。

cards.en:
Intuition: "due date" is not a fact about a student, and not a fact about a book. It is a fact about one borrowing of that book by that student.

The rule: attributes that depend on both entities belong to the relationship (drawn on the diamond) and, after resolving, to the associative entity.

  • Student–Borrow–Book: checkout date, due date, return date → CHECKOUT(SID, BID, CDATE, DDATE, RDATE).
  • Store–Sell–Book: stock, price (differ per store) → SELL(SID, ISBN, STOCK, PRICE).
  • Student–Enrol–Elective: score.

If the same pair can repeat (borrow the same book again), add the date to the key.

Exam wording: "The due date depends on both the student and the book, so it is an attribute of the relationship / associative entity."
cards.zh:
直觉：“到期日”既不是学生的事实，也不是书的事实，而是某次借阅的事实。

规则：依赖两边的属性属于关系（画在菱形上），拆开后属于关联实体。

  • 借书：借出日、到期日、归还日。
  • 书店卖书：库存、售价（每店不同）。
  • 选修：分数。

同一对可重复（再借同一本），把日期加入主键。

考试写法："The due date depends on both the student and the book, so it is an attribute of the relationship / associative entity."

ex.q: Where does SCORE go: STUDENT, ELECTIVE or ENROL?
ex.a:
1. A score belongs to one student in one subject.
  2. It depends on both → ENROL(SID, EID, SCORE).

ex.q: Ada borrows Dune twice. Why is the key of CHECKOUT (SID, BID, CDATE) and not (SID, BID)?
ex.a:
1. (1, 10) would appear twice → duplicate key.
  2. Adding CDATE makes each borrowing unique.
ex.az: 1. 同一对出现两次，加 CDATE 才唯一。

ex.q: A student puts PRICE in BOOK for Store M—Sell—N Book, while each store sets its own price.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: the price depends on the store and the book.
  2. In BOOK it can hold only one price for all stores.
  3. Put PRICE in SELL(SID, ISBN, STOCK, PRICE).
ex.az: 1. 错误：价格依赖店和书两者，应放 SELL。

demo.query: SELECT s.SNAME, b.TITLE, c.CDATE, c.DDATE, c.RDATE FROM CHECKOUT c JOIN STUDENT s ON c.SID = s.SID JOIN BOOK b ON c.BID = b.BID;
demo.note: Dates live in CHECKOUT: each row is one borrowing. Ada borrowed Dune twice, so CDATE is part of the key.

cards.en:
Using Student — Join — Sports event (character written next to the entity being counted):

Next to StudentNext to EventTypeHow to store
11one-to-oneFK in either table (or merge into an attribute)
1Mone-to-manyFK in EVENT (the many side)
M1many-to-oneFK in STUDENT
MNmany-to-manynew associative table with two FKs

Memory tip: "FK goes to the many side; M:N needs a middle table."

Exam wording: "1:M – the primary key of the one side is added to the many side as a foreign key. M:N – a new table is created containing the primary keys of both tables."
cards.zh:
以 Student — Join — Sports event 为例（字符写在被数的实体旁）：

Student 旁Event 旁类型存法
11一对一任一表放外键（或并为属性）
1M一对多外键放 EVENT
M1多对一外键放 STUDENT
MN多对多新建关联表

口诀：“外键去多的一边；多对多要中间表。”

考试写法：见英文。

ex.q: Next to Student: M, next to Event: 1. Describe it and store it.
ex.a:
1. 1 next to Event: each student joins at most one event.
  2. M next to Student: each event has many students.
  3. Many-to-one: FK EVENTID in STUDENT.
ex.az: 1. 每生最多一项，每项多人 → 外键放 STUDENT。

ex.q: Customer – Product (customers buy many products; a product is bought by many customers). How many tables?
ex.a:
1. M:N.
  2. CUSTOMER, PRODUCT + ORDER(associative) = 3.

ex.q: A student stores a 1:M relationship with an associative table "to be safe".
ex.a:
1. Mistake (inefficient): it works but adds an unnecessary table and join, and doesn't force 'at most one'.
  2. For 1:M, just put the FK in the many side.
ex.az: 1. 不佳：一对多不需要中间表，外键放 many 一方即可。

frames.en: School 1 — 1 Principal → FK PID in SCHOOL (either side).
Class 1 — M Student → FK CID in STUDENT.
Student M — N Elective → new table ENROLMENT(SID, EID).

cards.en:
Intuition: writing your home address on every page of your notebook. It wastes paper, and if you move, you must fix every page.

The rule: data redundancy refers to duplicated pieces of data that are redundant and occupy precious storage space. It is usually caused by a poorly designed database.

Example STUDENT table (primary key SID+EID):

SIDSNAMECLASSCTEACHEIDENAMEETEACHSCORE
03493Ada3AMrs Au2PhysicsMr Poon0
03496Clem3BMr Bao1HistoryMs Ho78
03496Clem3BMr Bao2PhysicsMr Poon98
03496Clem3BMr Bao3ICTMr Suen89
03505Eva3BMr Bao1HistoryMs Ho83
03510Finn3AMrs Au3ICTMr Suen71

"3B, Mr Bao" is stored 3 times (once per Clem's subject). "ICT, Mr Suen" is stored twice.

The bigger danger: redundancy causes three anomalies: update, insertion, deletion.

Exam wording: "Data redundancy refers to duplicated pieces of data that occupy storage space. It may cause update, insertion and deletion anomalies."
cards.zh:
直觉：每页笔记都写家庭地址：浪费纸，搬家要每页改。

规则：data redundancy 是重复多余、占用宝贵空间的数据，通常因设计不好造成。

SIDSNAMECLASSCTEACHEIDENAMEETEACHSCORE
03493Ada3AMrs Au2PhysicsMr Poon0
03496Clem3BMr Bao1HistoryMs Ho78
03496Clem3BMr Bao2PhysicsMr Poon98
03496Clem3BMr Bao3ICTMr Suen89
03505Eva3BMr Bao1HistoryMs Ho83
03510Finn3AMrs Au3ICTMr Suen71

“3B, Mr Bao” 存了 3 次；“ICT, Mr Suen” 存了 2 次。

更大的问题：冗余导致三种 anomalies：update、insertion、deletion。

考试写法："Data redundancy refers to duplicated pieces of data that occupy storage space. It may cause update, insertion and deletion anomalies."

ex.q: In the table above, how many times is Mr Bao (class teacher of 3B) stored?
ex.a:
1. Rows with CLASS 3B: Clem×3, Eva×1.
  2. 4 times. A good design stores it once.

ex.q: Which data is NOT redundant: SNAME, ETEACH or SCORE?
ex.a:
1. SNAME repeats per subject → redundant.
  2. ETEACH repeats per student → redundant.
  3. SCORE is one value per (student, subject) → not redundant.
ex.az: 1. SCORE 每对只一个 → 不冗余。

ex.q: A student says: "Two students both named Ada is data redundancy."
ex.a:
1. Mistake: same value ≠ same fact.
  2. Two different students who share a name are two different facts.
  3. Redundancy = the same fact stored more than once.
ex.az: 1. 错误：相同值不等于同一事实。

demo.setup:
CREATE TABLE STUDENT(SID CHAR(5), SNAME VARCHAR(20), CLASS CHAR(2), CTEACH VARCHAR(20), EID INT, ENAME VARCHAR(20), ETEACH VARCHAR(20), SCORE INT, PRIMARY KEY(SID,EID));
INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES('03493','Ada','3A','Mrs Au',2,'Physics','Mr Poon',0),('03496','Clem','3B','Mr Bao',1,'History','Ms Ho',78),('03496','Clem','3B','Mr Bao',2,'Physics','Mr Poon',98),('03496','Clem','3B','Mr Bao',3,'ICT','Mr Suen',89),('03505','Eva','3B','Mr Bao',1,'History','Ms Ho',83),('03510','Finn','3A','Mrs Au',3,'ICT','Mr Suen',71);
demo.query: SELECT CLASS, CTEACH, COUNT(*) AS TIMES_STORED FROM STUDENT GROUP BY CLASS, CTEACH;
demo.note: Each class teacher should be stored once, but 3B's teacher is stored 4 times.

cards.en:
Intuition: you change your phone number on one of your accounts but forget the others. Now people find two different numbers.

The rule: an update anomaly occurs when a database with data redundancy fails to maintain data consistency after an update. One real-world change needs many records updated; missing one leaves contradicting values.

  • Clem moves 3B → 3A: 3 records must change.
  • ICT teacher changes from Mr Suen to Mrs Lee: 2 records must change.

Changing a value stored only once (one score) causes no anomaly.

Exam wording: "Update anomaly: the same data is stored in many records, so all of them must be updated; otherwise data inconsistency occurs."
cards.zh:
直觉：只在一个账户改了电话号码，其他忘了改，别人看到两个号码。

规则：update anomaly：有冗余的数据库在更新后无法保持数据一致。一个现实改变要改多条记录，漏改就矛盾。

  • Clem 由 3B 转 3A：要改 3 条。
  • ICT 老师换人：要改 2 条。

只存一次的值（某个分数）改了不会有异常。

考试写法："Update anomaly: the same data is stored in many records, so all of them must be updated; otherwise data inconsistency occurs."

ex.q: Mr Bao is replaced by Ms Wu as class teacher of 3B. How many records change?
ex.a:
1. Rows where CLASS='3B': 4.
  2. All 4 must change; missing any → inconsistency.

ex.q: Write the SQL to make the change correctly in the redundant table.
ex.a:
1. UPDATE STUDENT SET CTEACH='Ms Wu' WHERE CLASS='3B';
  2. The WHERE uses CLASS, so every 3B row is changed.
ex.az: 1. 用 WHERE CLASS='3B' 一次改所有。

ex.q: Changing Clem's ICT score from 89 to 90. A student calls it an update anomaly.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: the score is stored in only one record (SID+EID).
  2. No duplicated copies → no anomaly.
ex.az: 1. 错误：分数只存一次，没有异常。

demo.query: SELECT SID, SNAME, EID, CLASS, CTEACH FROM STUDENT WHERE SID='03496';
demo.note: Clem moved to 3A, but only 1 of her 3 records was updated: she is now in 3A and 3B at the same time.

cards.en:
Intuition: a form says "Name and Elective are required". A new student who hasn't picked an elective cannot be registered at all.

The rule: an insertion anomaly is the inability to insert data of one entity type without having the data of another entity type.

Why: STUDENT's primary key is SID+EID, and a primary key field cannot be NULL.

  • New student Dio, no elective yet → EID NULL → cannot insert.
  • New subject Art, no students yet → SID NULL → cannot insert.

Exam wording: "Insertion anomaly: data of a new [student] cannot be inserted until there is data of [an elective], because the primary key cannot be NULL."
cards.zh:
直觉：表格要求“姓名和选修科必填”，还没选科的新生根本无法登记。

规则：insertion anomaly：没有另一实体的数据就无法插入某实体的数据。

原因：主键 SID+EID，主键字段不能为 NULL。

  • 新生 Dio 未选科 → EID 为 NULL → 不能插入。
  • 新科 Art 无学生 → SID 为 NULL → 不能插入。

考试写法：见英文。

ex.q: Can we insert class 3C with teacher Ms Ng before any student joins?
ex.a:
1. Class data lives only in student rows.
  2. A row needs SID and EID (PK) → none exist → cannot insert.

ex.q: Shop table PROD(PID, PNAME, SID, SNAME) with PK PID+SID. A new shop sells nothing yet.
ex.a:
1. PID would be NULL.
  2. Insertion anomaly: the shop cannot be added.

ex.q: A student fixes the problem by inserting Dio with EID = 0 (a fake subject).
ex.a:
1. Mistake: a fake value hides the anomaly but stores wrong data ("Dio takes subject 0").
  2. Counts and joins become wrong.
  3. Real fix: normalise so STUDENT(SID, ...) is separate from ENROL.
ex.az:
1. 错误：填假值会存入错误数据。
  2. 应规范化拆表。

notes.t: Try to add new student Dio, without any elective.
notes.tz: 尝试插入未选科的 Dio。

notes.t: EID is left out, so it becomes NULL.
Check: SQLite allowed the NULL (a quirk: SQLite permits NULL in composite keys unless NOT NULL is declared). Strict DBMSs such as MySQL reject this row, which is the insertion anomaly.
notes.tz: SQLite 有特例会接受 NULL；MySQL 等会拒绝，这就是插入异常。

code.in:
CREATE TABLE STUDENT(SID CHAR(5), SNAME VARCHAR(20), CLASS CHAR(2), CTEACH VARCHAR(20), EID INT, ENAME VARCHAR(20), ETEACH VARCHAR(20), SCORE INT, PRIMARY KEY(SID,EID));
INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES('03493','Ada','3A','Mrs Au',2,'Physics','Mr Poon',0),('03496','Clem','3B','Mr Bao',1,'History','Ms Ho',78),('03496','Clem','3B','Mr Bao',2,'Physics','Mr Poon',98),('03496','Clem','3B','Mr Bao',3,'ICT','Mr Suen',89),('03505','Eva','3B','Mr Bao',1,'History','Ms Ho',83),('03510','Finn','3A','Mrs Au',3,'ICT','Mr Suen',71);

demo.setup:
CREATE TABLE STUDENT(SID CHAR(5) NOT NULL, SNAME VARCHAR(20), CLASS CHAR(2), CTEACH VARCHAR(20), EID INT NOT NULL, ENAME VARCHAR(20), ETEACH VARCHAR(20), SCORE INT, PRIMARY KEY(SID,EID));
INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES('03493','Ada','3A','Mrs Au',2,'Physics','Mr Poon',0),('03496','Clem','3B','Mr Bao',1,'History','Ms Ho',78),('03496','Clem','3B','Mr Bao',2,'Physics','Mr Poon',98),('03496','Clem','3B','Mr Bao',3,'ICT','Mr Suen',89),('03505','Eva','3B','Mr Bao',1,'History','Ms Ho',83),('03510','Finn','3A','Mrs Au',3,'ICT','Mr Suen',71);
demo.query: SELECT DISTINCT ENAME FROM STUDENT;
demo.note: With SID and EID NOT NULL (like a real primary key), a new subject 'Art' with no student cannot be added: it can never appear in this list.

cards.en:
Intuition: you throw away an old receipt and lose the only copy of the shop's phone number written on it.

The rule: a deletion anomaly is the loss of data of one entity type when deleting the data of another entity type. One record holds facts about two things; deleting it removes both.

  • Every student of 3A (Ada, Finn) leaves → the class teacher of 3A (Mrs Au) is lost.
  • Clem and Eva drop History → teacher of History (Ms Ho) lost.
  • Eva drops her only subject → Eva's own name and class lost.

Exam wording: "Deletion anomaly: deleting the record of [a student] also deletes the only copy of [the subject's teacher], so that data is lost."
cards.zh:
直觉：扔掉旧收据，上面唯一一份店铺电话也没了。

规则：deletion anomaly：删除某实体的数据时，连带失去另一实体的数据。

  • 3A 唯一学生离校 → 3A 班主任资料丢失。
  • History 的学生都退选 → History 老师资料丢失。
  • Eva 退掉唯一一科 → 她自己的资料也丢失。

考试写法：见英文。

ex.q: Clem and Eva drop History. What is lost?
ex.a:
1. DELETE rows with EID=1 (Clem, Eva).
  2. No row with History remains → Ms Ho (History teacher) is lost.

ex.q: Retail: FastTech sells only Smartphone. Smartphone is discontinued and deleted.
ex.a:
1. The only record with FastTech is gone.
  2. All shop data of FastTech is lost → deletion anomaly.

ex.q: Deleting one of Clem's three subjects. A student calls it a deletion anomaly.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: Clem's data still exists in her other 2 rows, and Physics still has other students.
  2. Nothing else is lost → no anomaly.
ex.az: 1. 错误：没有其他资料丢失，不算异常。

demo.query: SELECT DISTINCT EID, ENAME, ETEACH FROM STUDENT;
demo.note: After Clem and Eva drop History (EID 1), History and its teacher Ms Ho have disappeared from the database.

cards.en:
Method: look at the action first, then what goes wrong.

ActionWhat goes wrongAnomaly
Change a fact stored in many recordssome copies missed → inconsistentUpdate
Add data of one entity alonepart of PK would be NULL → rejectedInsertion
Remove a recordanother entity's only copy disappearsDeletion

Traps:

  • Value stored in one record only → no anomaly.
  • "Adam no longer owns GG Garden" (only owner) → we delete a record → deletion, not update.
  • "Gabe changes his name" and Gabe has 2 records → update.

Exam wording: name the anomaly, the action, and the exact data affected.
cards.zh:
方法：先看动作，再看出什么问题。

动作问题异常
改多处存储的事实漏改 → 不一致Update
单独加某实体主键部分为 NULLInsertion
删记录其他实体唯一副本消失Deletion

陷阱：只存一次 → 无异常；“Adam 不再拥有物业”是删除；“Gabe 改名”且有两条 → 更新。

考试写法：写出异常名称、动作、受影响的数据。

ex.q: A new elective Art is offered but no one has chosen it. Which anomaly?
ex.a:
1. Action: add a subject alone.
  2. SID (PK part) would be NULL.
  3. Insertion anomaly.

ex.q: Mr Poon's name is corrected to 'Mr Pun'. Physics has 2 students.
ex.a:
1. Action: change a fact stored in 2 records.
  2. Update anomaly if one is missed.

ex.q: "Adam, the only owner of GG Garden, sells it." A student says update anomaly.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: the ownership record is deleted, not changed.
  2. GG Garden's data disappears with it → deletion anomaly.
ex.az: 1. 错误：是删除不是更新 → 删除异常。

frames.en: Fact copied in many rows; one row missed → update anomaly.
New entity has no partner; PK part NULL → insertion anomaly.
Removing a row removes another entity's only copy → deletion anomaly.

cards.en:
Intuition: tidy one messy drawer into labelled boxes: one box per kind of thing, linked by labels.

The rule: normalisation is designing a database in a way that

  • reduces data redundancy;
  • prevents occurrences of anomalies;
  • improves flexibility.

Levels: 1NF → 2NF → 3NF. Each level includes all rules of the one before (a 3NF table is also 2NF and 1NF).

In practice: split a big table into smaller related tables linked by foreign keys. Cost: queries need more joins.

Exam wording: "Normalisation reduces data redundancy, prevents anomalies and improves flexibility."
cards.zh:
直觉：把一个乱抽屉整理成多个贴好标签的盒子。

规则：normalisation：reduces data redundancy、prevents anomalies、improves flexibility。

级别 1NF → 2NF → 3NF，后一级包含前一级所有规则。

做法：把大表拆成多个相关小表，用外键连接。代价：查询要更多 join。

考试写法："Normalisation reduces data redundancy, prevents anomalies and improves flexibility."

ex.q: Normalise the 8-field STUDENT table. What tables result?
ex.a:
1. STUDENT(SID, SNAME, CLASS)
  2. CLASSLIST(CLASS, CTEACH)
  3. ELECTIVE(EID, ENAME, ETEACH)
  4. ENROL(SID, EID, SCORE)

ex.q: After normalising, how many records change when Mr Bao is replaced?
ex.a:
1. CTEACH is stored once in CLASSLIST.
  2. 1 record.

ex.q: A student says: "Normalisation always makes the database faster."
ex.a:
1. Mistake: normalisation makes updates safe, but queries need more joins and can be slower.
  2. That is why denormalisation exists.
ex.az: 1. 错误：查询要更多 join，可能更慢。

demo.query: SELECT s.SNAME, c.CTEACH, e.ENAME, n.SCORE FROM STUDENT s JOIN CLASSLIST c ON s.CLASS=c.CLASS JOIN ENROL n ON s.SID=n.SID JOIN ELECTIVE e ON n.EID=e.EID;
demo.note: Same information as the big table, but each fact is stored once in 4 tables. Getting it back needs 3 joins.

cards.en:
Intuition: one box, one item. Don't squeeze a list into one cell, and don't make "slot 1, slot 2, slot 3" columns.

Rules of 1NF:

  1. Every attribute must not contain multiple values.
  2. There must not be any repeating attributes.
  • Multiple values: ENAME = 'History,Physics,ICT'.
  • Repeating attributes: ELEC1, ELEC2, ELEC3; LM1, LM2, LM3; one Yes/No field per subject. Each cell has one value, but it is still not 1NF.

Why it matters: a fixed maximum (only 3 slots), and hard queries (string search, many ORs).

Exam wording: "The table is not in 1NF because the attribute [X] contains multiple values / [X1, X2, X3] are repeating attributes."
cards.zh:
直觉：一格一物。不要把列表塞进一格，也不要开“槽 1、槽 2、槽 3”。

1NF 规则：1. 每个属性不能有多个值；2. 不能有重复属性。

  • 多值：ENAME='History,Physics,ICT'。
  • 重复属性：ELEC1/2/3、LM1/2/3；每格虽只一值，仍不是 1NF。

考试写法："The table is not in 1NF because the attribute [X] contains multiple values / [X1, X2, X3] are repeating attributes."

ex.q: CITY(CTID, CTNAME, LM1, LM2, LM3). 1NF?
ex.a:
1. LM1–LM3 store the same kind of data (landmarks).
  2. Repeating attributes → not 1NF.

ex.q: ACTOR row with AWARD = 'Best Actress (IFCS), Best Actress (OFCS)'. 1NF?
ex.a:
1. One cell holds two awards.
  2. Multiple values → not 1NF.

ex.q: ELEC1, ELEC2, ELEC3 each hold only one subject code. A student says "one value per cell, so it is 1NF".
ex.a:
1. Mistake: forgetting rule 2.
  2. ELEC1–3 are repeating attributes → not 1NF.
ex.az: 1. 错误：忘了规则 2，重复属性也违反 1NF。

demo.setup:
CREATE TABLE S(SID TEXT, NAME TEXT, ELEC1 TEXT, ELEC2 TEXT, ELEC3 TEXT);
INSERT INTO S VALUES('03493','Ada','Physics',NULL,NULL),('03496','Clem','History','Physics','ICT'),('03505','Eva','History',NULL,NULL);
demo.query: SELECT NAME FROM S WHERE ELEC1='ICT' OR ELEC2='ICT' OR ELEC3='ICT';
demo.note: Repeating attributes: to find ICT students you must check 3 columns, and a 4th subject would need a new column.

cards.en:
Steps:

  1. Multiple values → split so each value is in its own record. The new primary key = old key + that attribute (e.g. SID+ENAME).
  2. Repeating attributes → turn each into its own record, or move them into a new table with a foreign key: LANDMARK(LMID, LMNAME, CTID).

Counting records: new count = old count + extra values. ACTOR has 7 records; 2 records hold 2 awards each → 7 + 2 = 9.

The new LANDMARK table is more flexible: a city can have any number of landmarks.

Exam wording: "Store each value in a separate record." / "Move the repeating attributes into a new table with a foreign key."
cards.zh:
步骤：

  1. 多值 → 拆成每值一条记录；新主键 = 旧主键 + 该属性。
  2. 重复属性 → 变成多条记录，或移到新表加外键：LANDMARK(LMID, LMNAME, CTID)。

数记录：新数目 = 旧数目 + 额外值。ACTOR 7 条，2 条各有 2 个奖 → 9 条。

考试写法："Store each value in a separate record."

ex.q: Clem's row has ENAME='History,Physics,ICT'; Ada 'Physics'; Eva 'History'. How many rows after 1NF?
ex.a:
1. Clem → 3 rows; Ada 1; Eva 1.
  2. 3 + 2 = 5 rows (old 3 + 2 extra).
  3. PK becomes SID+ENAME.

ex.q: Convert CITY(CTID, CTNAME, LM1, LM2, LM3) into 1NF with a new table.
ex.a:
1. CITY(CTID, CTNAME)
  2. LANDMARK(LMID, LMNAME, CTID), CTID references CITY.

ex.q: After splitting Clem into 3 rows, a student keeps SID as the primary key.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: SID '03496' now appears 3 times → not unique.
  2. The key must be SID+ENAME.

frames.en: Clem | 'History,Physics,ICT' (3 values in one cell).

Clem | History
Clem | Physics
Clem | ICT
SID alone repeats → primary key becomes SID + ENAME.

cards.en:
Intuition: if you know a student's ID, you know their name. The ID determines the name.

The rule: a functional dependency exists between two sets of attributes when the values of one set can be uniquely determined by the values of another set. Write X → Y: "X determines Y".

  • SID → {SNAME, CLASS}
  • CLASS → CTEACH (class tells you the teacher, not the student)
  • EID → {ENAME, ETEACH}
  • {SID, EID} → SCORE (needs both)

Dependencies come from the meaning of the data, not just a few sample rows.

Exam wording: "CTEACH is functionally dependent on CLASS, because each class has exactly one class teacher."
cards.zh:
直觉：知道学号就知道姓名：学号决定姓名。

规则：若一组属性的值能唯一确定另一组属性的值，就存在 functional dependency，写作 X → Y。

  • SID → {SNAME, CLASS}
  • CLASS → CTEACH
  • EID → {ENAME, ETEACH}
  • {SID, EID} → SCORE

依据数据的意义，不是几行样本。

考试写法："CTEACH is functionally dependent on CLASS, because each class has exactly one class teacher."

ex.q: Does SNAME → SID hold?
ex.a:
1. Two students can share a name.
  2. A name does not uniquely give one SID → no.

ex.q: Write the FDs for ORDERLINE(OID, PID, PNAME, QTY).
ex.a:
1. PID → PNAME.
  2. {OID, PID} → QTY.

ex.q: Sample data: every student with score 98 is named Clem. A student writes SCORE → SNAME.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: a coincidence in sample rows is not a rule.
  2. Another student could also score 98. FDs come from meaning.

demo.setup:
CREATE TABLE STUDENT(SID CHAR(5), SNAME VARCHAR(20), CLASS CHAR(2), CTEACH VARCHAR(20), EID INT, ENAME VARCHAR(20), ETEACH VARCHAR(20), SCORE INT, PRIMARY KEY(SID,EID));
INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES('03493','Ada','3A','Mrs Au',2,'Physics','Mr Poon',0),('03496','Clem','3B','Mr Bao',1,'History','Ms Ho',78),('03496','Clem','3B','Mr Bao',2,'Physics','Mr Poon',98),('03496','Clem','3B','Mr Bao',3,'ICT','Mr Suen',89),('03505','Eva','3B','Mr Bao',1,'History','Ms Ho',83),('03510','Finn','3A','Mrs Au',3,'ICT','Mr Suen',71);
demo.query: SELECT CLASS, COUNT(DISTINCT CTEACH) AS TEACHERS_PER_CLASS FROM STUDENT GROUP BY CLASS;
demo.note: Checking CLASS → CTEACH: every class maps to exactly 1 teacher, consistent with the dependency.

cards.en:
Intuition: a score needs the student and the subject (whole key). A name only needs the student (half the key).

Full functional dependency: all non-primary key attributes depend on the (whole) primary key. ELECTIVE(EID, ENAME, ETEACH).

Partial functional dependency: some non-primary key attributes depend on part of the primary key. STUDENT with PK SID+EID:

  • SID → {SNAME, CLASS, CTEACH} (part)
  • EID → {ENAME, ETEACH} (part)
  • {SID, EID} → SCORE (whole)

Key point: partial dependency is only possible with a composite key. A 1NF table with a single-field key is automatically 2NF.

Exam wording: "SNAME depends on SID only, which is part of the primary key SID+EID, so it is a partial functional dependency."
cards.zh:
直觉：分数要学生和科目（整个主键）；姓名只要学生（半个主键）。

完全相关：所有非主键属性依赖整个主键。

部分相关：某些非主键属性只依赖主键的一部分（例：SID → SNAME）。

重点：只有复合主键才可能有部分相关；单字段主键的 1NF 表自动是 2NF。

考试写法："SNAME depends on SID only, which is part of the primary key SID+EID, so it is a partial functional dependency."

ex.q: ENROL(<u>SID, EID</u>, SCORE). Partial dependency?
ex.a:
1. SCORE needs both SID and EID.
  2. Full dependency only → no partial.

ex.q: ORDERLINE(<u>OID, PID</u>, PNAME, QTY). Find the partial dependency.
ex.a:
1. PID → PNAME; PID is part of the key.
  2. PNAME is partially dependent.

ex.q: STUDENT(<u>SID</u>, SNAME, CLASS, CTEACH). A student says CTEACH is partially dependent.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: the key is a single field, so there is no 'part' of the key.
  2. CLASS → CTEACH is a transitive dependency (next cards), not partial.
ex.az: 1. 错误：单字段主键没有“部分”，这是传递相关。

frames.en: Primary key = SID + EID.
SNAME needs only SID → partial. ENAME needs only EID → partial.
SCORE needs SID and EID → full.

cards.en:
Rules of 2NF:

  1. Follows all rules of 1NF.
  2. There must NOT be any partial functional dependency.

Every non-key attribute must depend on the whole key.

How: write the FDs, make one table per determinant:

  • SID → {SNAME, CLASS, CTEACH} → STUDENT(SID, SNAME, CLASS, CTEACH)
  • EID → {ENAME, ETEACH} → ELECTIVE(EID, ENAME, ETEACH)
  • {SID, EID} → SCORE → ENROL(SID, EID, SCORE)

Result (Activity 5.2): cancel ICT → no deletion anomaly; rename Gabe → 1 record; new student → insert directly.

Exam wording: "The table is not in 2NF because [SNAME] depends only on [SID], which is part of the primary key."
cards.zh:
2NF 规则：1. 满足 1NF；2. 没有部分功能相关。

方法：写出 FD，每个决定因素一个表：STUDENT、ELECTIVE、ENROL。

结果：取消 ICT 无删除异常；Gabe 改名改 1 条；新生可直接插入。

考试写法："The table is not in 2NF because [SNAME] depends only on [SID], which is part of the primary key."

ex.q: Normalise ORDERLINE(<u>OID, PID</u>, PNAME, QTY) to 2NF.
ex.a:
1. PID → PNAME (partial).
  2. PRODUCT(PID, PNAME)
  3. ORDERLINE(OID, PID, QTY)

ex.q: After 2NF, can we insert new student Dio with no elective?
ex.a:
1. Yes: insert into STUDENT(SID, ...) only.
  2. No EID needed → insertion anomaly solved.

ex.q: A student moves SCORE into STUDENT(<u>SID</u>, SNAME, ..., SCORE) while making 2NF.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: SCORE depends on SID and EID.
  2. In STUDENT, one student could hold only one score.
  3. SCORE stays in ENROL(SID, EID, SCORE).
ex.az: 1. 错误：SCORE 依赖两者，应留在 ENROL。

code.src:
INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES ('03520', 'Dio', '3B');
SELECT * FROM STUDENT WHERE SID = '03520';

notes.t: After normalising, a new student is inserted without any elective.
notes.tz: 规范化后，可直接插入未选科的新生。

notes.t: Dio is stored: no insertion anomaly.
notes.tz: Dio 已存入，无插入异常。

frames.en: STUDENT(<u>SID, EID</u>, SNAME, CLASS, CTEACH, ENAME, ETEACH, SCORE)

SID → SNAME, CLASS, CTEACH
EID → ENAME, ETEACH
SID, EID → SCORE

STUDENT(SID, SNAME, CLASS, CTEACH)
ELECTIVE(EID, ENAME, ETEACH)
ENROL(SID, EID, SCORE)

cards.en:
Intuition: "I know a guy who knows a guy." The student ID gives the class, and the class gives the class teacher.

The rule: transitive functional dependency: some non-primary key attributes are dependent on other non-primary key attributes.

STUDENT(SID, SNAME, CLASS, CTEACH): SID → CLASS and CLASS → CTEACH, so SID → CTEACH only through CLASS.

Effect: CTEACH repeats for every student of the class → redundancy, update anomaly.

More: FID → GENRE → GDESC; CTID → CC → {CNAME, HOS, CONTINENT}.

Exam wording: "CTEACH depends on CLASS, which is a non-primary key attribute, so there is a transitive functional dependency."
cards.zh:
直觉：“朋友的朋友”。学号给出班别，班别给出班主任。

规则：传递功能相关：某些非主键属性依赖于其他非主键属性。

SID → CLASS → CTEACH，CTEACH 经由 CLASS 依赖 SID。

后果：每个学生都重复班主任 → 冗余、更新异常。

考试写法："CTEACH depends on CLASS, which is a non-primary key attribute, so there is a transitive functional dependency."

ex.q: FILM(<u>FID</u>, FNAME, GENRE, GDESC). Find the transitive dependency.
ex.a:
1. FID → GENRE (key → non-key).
  2. GENRE → GDESC (non-key → non-key).
  3. So FID → GENRE → GDESC is transitive.

ex.q: COURSE(<u>CID</u>, CNAME, FID, FNAME), FID = faculty ID.
ex.a:
1. FID → FNAME, FID is not the key.
  2. CID → FID → FNAME: transitive.

ex.q: ENROL(<u>SID, EID</u>, SCORE, GRADE) where GRADE is calculated from SCORE. A student says there is no transitive dependency because the key is composite.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: transitive dependency can happen with any key.
  2. SCORE → GRADE is non-key → non-key → transitive.
ex.az: 1. 错误：复合主键也可有传递相关。

frames.en: SID → CLASS (key → non-key).
CLASS → CTEACH (non-key → non-key).
SID → CTEACH only via CLASS: transitive.
frames.zh: 经由 CLASS → 传递相关。

cards.en:
Rules of 3NF:

  1. Follows all rules of 2NF.
  2. There must NOT be any transitive functional dependency.

Every non-key attribute depends on the key, the whole key and nothing but the key.

How: move the transitively dependent attributes into a new table whose key is the middle attribute; keep that attribute as a foreign key.

STUDENT(SID, SNAME, CLASS, CTEACH) → STUDENT(SID, SNAME, CLASS) + CLASSLIST(CLASS, CTEACH).

Benefit: a new class teacher updates one record.

Exam wording: "Move CTEACH into a new table CLASSLIST(CLASS, CTEACH), with CLASS in STUDENT as a foreign key."
cards.zh:
3NF 规则：1. 满足 2NF；2. 没有传递功能相关。

非主键属性只依赖主键。

方法：把传递相关的属性移到新表，新表主键是中间属性，并在原表保留它做外键。

STUDENT → STUDENT(SID, SNAME, CLASS) + CLASSLIST(CLASS, CTEACH)。

好处：换班主任只改一条。

考试写法：见英文。

ex.q: Normalise FILM(<u>FID</u>, FNAME, GENRE, GDESC) to 3NF.
ex.a:
1. GENRE → GDESC is transitive.
  2. FILM(FID, FNAME, GENRE), GENRE is FK.
  3. GENRE(GENRE, GDESC).

ex.q: CITY(<u>CTID</u>, CTNAME, TIMEZONE, AREA, POPULATION, CC, CNAME, HOS, CONTINENT).
ex.a:
1. CC → {CNAME, HOS, CONTINENT} transitive.
  2. CITY(CTID, CTNAME, TIMEZONE, AREA, POPULATION, CC)
  3. COUNTRY(CC, CNAME, HOS, CONTINENT)

ex.q: A student makes CLASSLIST(<u>CLASS</u>, CTEACH) but deletes CLASS from STUDENT.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: without CLASS in STUDENT, we no longer know which class a student is in.
  2. CLASS must stay in STUDENT as a foreign key.
ex.az: 1. 错误：CLASS 要留在 STUDENT 做外键。

notes.t: In 3NF the class teacher is changed in ONE record only.
Show each 3B student's class teacher.
notes.tz: 显示 3B 学生的班主任。

notes.t: Join STUDENT to CLASSLIST by the foreign key CLASS.
Only class 3B: both students now show Ms Wu, consistent.
notes.tz: 两人都显示 Ms Wu，一致。

frames.en: STUDENT(<u>SID</u>, SNAME, CLASS, CTEACH)
CLASS → CTEACH (non-key → non-key).
STUDENT(<u>SID</u>, SNAME, CLASS) + CLASSLIST(<u>CLASS</u>, CTEACH). CLASS stays as FK.

cards.en:
Rule1NF2NF3NF
No multiple values in an attribute✓✓✓
No repeating attributes✓✓✓
No partial functional dependency✓✓
No transitive functional dependency✓
  • Partial FD: non-key depends on part of the primary key.
  • Transitive FD: non-key depends on another non-key.

Exam method: (1) any lists or ELEC1/ELEC2? → not 1NF. (2) composite key and a field depending on part? → not 2NF. (3) a non-key determining another non-key? → not 3NF. Always name the attributes.

Exam wording: "The table is in 2NF but not 3NF because [B] depends on [A], a non-primary key attribute."
cards.zh:
规则1NF2NF3NF
无多值✓✓✓
无重复属性✓✓✓
无部分相关✓✓
无传递相关✓

答题方法：依次查 1NF、2NF（只在复合主键时）、3NF，并写出具体属性名。

考试写法："The table is in 2NF but not 3NF because [B] depends on [A], a non-primary key attribute."

ex.q: BOOK(<u>ISBN</u>, TITLE, PUBID, PUBNAME). Highest normal form?
ex.a:
1. No lists → 1NF.
  2. Single key → 2NF.
  3. PUBID → PUBNAME (non-key→non-key) → not 3NF.
  4. Answer: 2NF.

ex.q: LOAN(<u>MID, BID, LDATE</u>, MNAME, DUEDATE). Highest NF?
ex.a:
1. 1NF ✓.
  2. MID → MNAME (part of key) → partial → not 2NF.
  3. Answer: 1NF.

ex.q: A student says a table is in 3NF because it has no transitive dependency, without checking 1NF/2NF.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: 3NF requires all 2NF and 1NF rules too.
  2. A table with ELEC1–3 and no transitive FD is still not 3NF.

frames.en: Any multiple values or repeating attributes? No → 1NF.
Composite key? Any field depending on part of it? No → 2NF.
Any non-key → non-key? No → 3NF.

cards.en:
ACTOR(ID, NAME, SEX, DOB, FID, FNAME, RNAME, FYEAR, GENRE, AWARD), primary key ID+FID, 7 records.

(a) 1NF? No: AWARD holds multiple values (roles Maya and Ted each have 2 awards). Split: 7 + 2 = 9 records.

(b) 2NF? FDs: ID → {NAME, SEX, DOB}; FID → {FNAME, FYEAR, GENRE}; {ID, FID} → {RNAME, AWARD}. NAME depends on ID, part of the key → partial → not 2NF.

(c) 3NF: ACTOR(ID, NAME, SEX, DOB); FILM(FID, FNAME, FYEAR, GENRE); ROLE(ID, FID, RNAME, AWARD).
